text:
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled in 2h -> prod: v2.14.0 (staging -> prod). Changes: serving kernel patch, quantization tweaks. scheduled_by: emma

emma: heads-up — this overlaps with the active EU DB incident, should we proceed?

raj: we should hold. DB incident is causing timeouts for eu region, risking higher error surface :warning:

deploy-bot: auto-hold triggered by incident-monitor: hold applied to release v2.14.0 -> prod. Canary paused at 0%.

oliver: +1 on hold. Question: do we pin prod back to 2.13.7 and rollback any partial canaries that landed?

casey: product approves pin/rollback. need stable behavior for customer flows today.

maria: propose a controlled rollback. Command for ops run:```bash
redwood deploy rollback --service=serving --to-version=2.13.7 --region=eu --grace-period=300
```

raj: +1. Also please disable autoscaling burst during rollback window to limit noisy neighbour effects.

emma: I'll update the release notes: "v2.14.0 -> prod paused due to incident; rollback to 2.13.7 initiated for eu."

oliver: Ops will execute rollback and monitor errors + SLOs. If stable for 30m we can consider reschedule.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued (id: rb-1932109876-1). Notifying oncall.

casey: reschedule proposal: new change window 2026-03-21 02:00 UTC. Rollout plan: staggered canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 15m observation waits.

maria: add fallback/pinning to rollout config: `rolloutStrategy: staggered, steps: [5,25,100], fallback: 2.13.7`

emma: confirmed. I'll update the calendar change window and send a short customer advisory to early-alpha list.

raj: filing post-incident release checklist + postmortem ticket: https://redwood.internal/ops/1923

oliver: once incident cleared, re-run canary smoke tests against eu before unhold. Make sure KV cache warming is included.

deploy-bot: thread paused for updates. Will publish status when rollback completes or if schedule changes. :white_check_mark:
